glosses: to put in a mood, to make one feel
to tune (e.g. a musical instrument)
nadawać właściwy ton instrumentowi muzycznemu

examples.text: …myśl o nocy na tym cmentarzu nieszczególnie mnie nastraja

glosses: wprowadzić kogoś w jakiś nastrój; powodować dane samopoczucie u kogoś
A melody.

examples.text: Eric played a catchy tune on his acoustic guitar and Alyssa played the drums.

glosses: A song, or short musical composition.
The act of tuning or maintenance.

examples.text: Your engine needs a good tune.

glosses: The state or condition of being correctly tuned.

examples.text: Your engine is now in tune.
This piano is not in tune.

glosses: Temper; frame of mind.
A sound; a note; a tone.

examples.text: Pray you now, if it may the ſtand with the tune of your voices, that I may bee Conſull, I haue heere the Cuſtomarie Gowne.

glosses: Order; harmony; concord.

examples.text: A child will learn three times as much when he is in tune, as when he […] is dragged unwillingly to [his task].

glosses: Used to show appreciation or approval of a song.

examples.text: You heard the new Rizzle Kicks song? — Tune!

glosses: To adjust (a musical instrument) so that it produces the correct pitches.

examples.text: to tune a piano or a violin
The Harpe. […] A harper with his wreſt maye tune the harpe wrong / Mys tunying of an Inſtrument ſhal hurt a true ſonge

She bids me hope; oh Heav'ns; ſhe pities me! / And pity ſtill foreruns approching love; / As Lightning does the Thunder! Tune your Harps / Ye Angels to that ſound; and thou, my Heart, / Make room to entertain thy flowing Joy.
Fortune foretun'd the Dying Notes of Rome: / Till I, thy Conſul ſole, conſol'd thy Doom.

glosses: To adjust or modify (especially a mechanical or electrical device) so that it functions optimally.

examples.text: Tuning the engine gave me an extra twenty horsepower.
Tune your mind, and anything becomes possible.

glosses: To adjust the frequency on a radio or TV set, so as to receive the desired channel.

examples.text: Tune to Channel 6 for all your favourite daytime shows.

glosses: Of faculties, senses, etc.: to adapt to or direct towards a particular target.

examples.text: My ears were tuned to the sounds of the forest.

glosses: To make more precise, intense, or effective; to put into a proper state or disposition.

examples.text: [H]ee hath incurred the euerlaſting diſpleaſure of the King, who had euen tun'd his bounty to ſing happineſſe to him.

glosses: To attune; to adapt in style of music; to make harmonious.

examples.text: For now to ſorrow must I tune my ſong, / And ſet my Harpe to notes of ſaddeſt wo, […]

glosses: To give a certain tone or character to.
To set (lyrics) to music.

examples.text: Ginsberg sang some poems from William Blake which he had "tuned".

glosses: To sing with melody or harmony.

examples.text: To ſee great Hercules whipping a Gigge, / And profound Sallomon to tune a Iigge.
Fountains and yee, that warble, as ye flow, / Melodious murmurs, warbling tune his praiſe.

glosses: To be impudent towards; to cheek.

examples.text: Are you tuning me?

glosses: to adjust the parameters of singing voice synthesis software such as VOCALOID (in order to achieve certain singing techniques, increase the human quality of the voice, etc.)

examples.text: […] Those who are highly skilled in manipulating the Vocaloid technology—e.g., tuning Miku's singing voices—arrange existing[…]
LOLA's voice is used simply to render basic notes and words with no pitch or expression tuning applied.
This compiling of a track holds many parallels with “tuning” a Miku track, […]

glosses: To eliminate or to get rid of something.

examples.text: I dispose of my trash in the garbage can.

glosses: To distribute or arrange; to put in place.

examples.text: Now, dear soldiers, march away: / And how thou pleasest, God, dispose the day!
Marianne’s pianoforte was unpacked and properly disposed of, and Elinor’s drawing were affixed to the walls of their sitting rooms.
I sat down within three feet of the entrance door, and I had no sooner got disposed than the door opened and a man came in[…].
By disposing the driving power over a number of cars instead of concentrating it in a single locomotive a great advance was made towards a high rate of acceleration.

glosses: To deal out; to assign to a use.

examples.text: what he designed to bestow on her funeral, he would rather dispose among the poor

glosses: To incline.

examples.text: In these uncertain times, I am disposed towards caution.
Endure and conquer; Jove will soon dispose / To future good our past and present woes.
They [suspicions] dispose kings to tyranny, husbands to jealousy, and wise men to irresolution and melancholy.

At twilight in the summer[…]the mice come out. They[…]eat the luncheon crumbs. Mr. Checkly, for instance, always brought his dinner in a paper parcel in his coat-tail pocket, and ate it when so disposed, sprinkling crumbs lavishly[…]on the floor.

glosses: To bargain; to make terms.

examples.text: She had disposed with Caesar.

glosses: To regulate; to adjust; to settle; to determine.

examples.text: the knightly forms of combat to dispose

glosses: The disposal or management of something.

examples.text: By thus doing, he submits himself to God's rod, commits himself to the dispose of his providence; yea, by thus doing, he casteth the lot of his present and future condition into the lap of his creditors, and leaves the whole dispose thereof to the Lord […]

glosses: Behaviour; disposition.
